The lipophilic steroid danazol, despite poor aqueous solubility, reached 46-67% absolute oral bioavailability in the fed state, supporting that steroid-like lipophilic compounds can exceed the 20% threshold.
Lipophilic drugs with challenging physicochemical profiles (lefamulin, tacrolimus) have absolute oral bioavailability of about 20-26%, at or above the threshold.
No visible L1 record provides affirmative evidence of F < 20% for a transferable context; the only borderline value (tacrolimus ~20%) still meets the threshold.

Acid lability of the 1,3-dioxolane ring and hepatic first-pass metabolism of the corticosteroid side chain are not quantified in the visible records.
Transfer from cardiac glycosides, bile acids, estrogens, and nonsteroid lipophilic drugs is structural-class analogy rather than direct query-specific evidence.

sampling context together.

visible structure, endpoint, assay, species, formulation, exposure, and
condition. Infer direction from the record cards first, then judge transfer from
